ci_method: Paired day-level bootstrap: the service dates on which either itinerary has a paired outcome are resampled with replacement (10,000 times, seed 20261124); each itinerary's feasibility rate is computed on the drawn dates where it has an outcome, and the interval is the central 95% of the differences. A showcase also needs both itineraries observed on at least the minimum sample size of the same dates. Resampling whole dates keeps the correlation between itineraries flying on the same day (shared weather and congestion), as FR-029 requires.
limitations: Airlines sometimes hold an outbound flight for connecting passengers. The data cannot show this, so some days classified as insufficient time may have worked in practice.
Gate changes and the walking distance between gates are not in the data.
How full flights were is not considered: a feasible connection does not mean a seat was available.
Transfer time is assumed (the hub's minimum connection time), not measured.
Results are historical frequencies for the data period, not a prediction of future connection feasibility.
Weather is measured only through BTS weather-attributed delays and weather cancellations; weather recorded under National Aviation System delays is not counted.

Many comparisons are made, each at the stated confidence level, with no multiple-comparison correction, so a single example can be a chance result; the decision rests on the number and spread of examples.

Sold routings come from DB1B, a 10% ticket sample: a routing sold rarely may have fewer sampled passengers than the minimum and be left out. DB1B records the selling airline, not the flight numbers, so a sold routing qualifies every flight pair on it that meets the other rules.

Itineraries are identified by schedule slot, whatever the flight numbers, but each slot must be scheduled on most days. Airlines whose departure times vary by day of week or season, such as Southwest, therefore have fewer itineraries than their sold passengers suggest; the report lists itineraries per airline.
